posts.excerpt: StrongLifts is $59.99 a year now, with no free tier. Kiron's Beginner 5×5 still works out every weight for {{kiron:price-annual}}, starting you light, with {{kiron:program-count}} programs for when it stalls.

posts.excerpt: Runna's strength sessions are built to make you a sturdier runner. Kiron runs a full lifting program with your runs on the same calendar, for {{kiron:price-annual}} against Runna's $119.99.

posts.title: Ladder App Alternative: Ladder vs Kiron on Price, Android and Flexibility
posts.excerpt: Ladder sells a coach for $179.99 a year, on iPhone only. Kiron is {{kiron:price-annual}} on {{kiron:cell-platforms}}, and plans your training from one of {{kiron:program-count}} ready-made programs or your own.

posts.title: Hevy vs Kiron: A Free Workout Log, or an App That Runs Your Plan?
posts.excerpt: Hevy is a very good log, free or $23.99 a year. Kiron is {{kiron:price-annual}} and plans for you: a proven program or your own, weights explained, and runs on the same calendar.

posts.title: Strong App Alternatives in 2026, and When to Stay With Strong
posts.excerpt: Strong is a fast log for routines you write. Kiron keeps the same do-the-next-workout habit but writes the plan and works out every weight, from one of {{kiron:program-count}} ready-made programs or yours.

posts.title: Workout Apps for Following a Program (Yours, a Coach's, or ChatGPT's)
posts.excerpt: The question that sorts workout apps is who writes the plan. Eight apps grouped by that job, from simple logs to coach-led teams, and Kiron, which runs one of {{kiron:program-count}} ready-made programs or the plan you already have.
